extra_misconceptions.fact: Robbery involves taking property directly from a person using force or threat, whereas burglary is unlawful entry to commit a felony.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burglary and robbery are interchangeable legal terms for stealing personal property from a residence or business.

extra_misconceptions.fact: White-collar crimes drain billions of dollars from pensions, raise consumer prices, and destroy public trust in financial institutions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Crime prevention proactively removes criminal opportunities and addresses root social causes before an offense ever takes place.

extra_misconceptions.fact: News outlets disproportionately cover rare violent offenses, whereas property crimes make up the vast majority of actual incidents.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Evening television broadcasts and social media feeds reflect the actual statistical frequency of local crime categories.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many crimes go unreported to police, so researchers pair FBI crime data with the National Crime Victimization Survey.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Official police arrest statistics capture every single criminal offense committed within a jurisdiction each calendar year.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The legacy Hierarchy Rule counted only the single most serious offense per incident, whereas NIBRS logs each individual offense.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gang membership drastically increases a young person's risk of violent victimization, felony conviction, and early mortality.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Joining a street gang provides youth with reliable personal protection and financial security against neighborhood violence.
